sampling_model.design: No sampling model is imposed; the input is one fixed compatible positive rational observational table.
sampling_model.units: A finite acyclic quasi-Markovian SCM with discrete observed alphabets of size at most \(q\).
sampling_model.treatment: A fixed intervention assignment touching at least three C-components.
sampling_model.overlap: Every observational joint cell has strictly positive probability; endpoint response types may have zero mass.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. Statistical projection and confidence-region optimization are outside the estimand and algorithm.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For degree at least three, the method is guaranteed to converge to a stationary point.
Spatial branch-and-bound maintains valid outer bounds and certifies epsilon-sharpness before global convergence.
Quasi-Markovian SCMs map exactly to local credal sets, with compact construction for a characterized subclass.
Bucket elimination is complete and has complexity exponential in induced width.
The response-function method gives tight symbolic bounds for a characterized linear-program class.
For a single intervention, column generation yields a polynomial-cardinality response representation.
Exact counterfactual credal inference is NP-hard even on polytrees outside the tractable subclass.
Untrusted univariate algebraic certificates can be checked inside Isabelle/HOL.
Rectangular local transition sets give sharp dynamic-regime bounds by backward induction.
The causaloptim interface computes tight symbolic bounds for its supported linear graph-and-query class.

body.tldr: For the headline subcase \(\mathfrak I_{q,k}^{\ge3}\) of the cardinality-unrestricted superclass \(\mathfrak J_{q,k}\), raw observational rows bound every original response block by \(q^2(k+1)\) coordinates. Every local and equality-factor feasible set is first posed in a finite-dimensional real space by an explicit rational H-representation; separate lemmas establish boundedness, compactness, rational extreme points, and \(O(B^2)\) coordinate encoding before support enumeration. Connected equality splitting preserves width and block-affinity, so standard min-sum and max-sum elimination computes exact sharp multi-intervention endpoints, rational attaining SCMs, and skeptical replay certificates in \(2^{O(q^2(k+1)^2)}\operatorname{poly}(B)\) bit operations. Independently of width, a binary query involving \(\ell\ge1\) original response blocks is solved by enumerating complete vertex lists for only \(\ell-1\) blocks and optimizing the last block by exact rational linear programming, giving \(B^{O((\ell-1)(1+\log B)^2)}\operatorname{poly}(B)\) bit operations and a polynomial-time elbow at \(\ell=1\). The genuine open step is executable serialized refinement with universal compatible-SCM validity and endpoint realization.

project_justification.gap: Higher-degree quasi-Markovian causal bounds are addressed by stationary-point search or general epsilon-sharp polynomial optimization. Their broad admissible program classes strictly contain the semantic image of the present explicit rational bounded-width class, but neither source gives exact endpoint and skeptical-certificate guarantees on that common image. Existing column-generation work also does not supply the fully expanded several-relevant-block guarantee or its one-block rational-LP elbow.
project_justification.niche: Small discrete multi-intervention queries often already materialize response columns and raw equalities, so their scalar interaction graph can be narrow even though the causal graph, objective degree, or canonical latent cardinality alone gives no tractability guarantee. When measured width is large, a binary query may still involve only a few original response blocks.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies explicit rational H-representations in real ambient spaces, proves factor boundedness and rational vertex encoding before enumeration, proves the raw clique bound and exact within-block gluing, and then derives exact bounded-width elimination and an abstract mathematical certificate theorem. Its secondary no-width algorithm enumerates complete supports for only all but one relevant binary block and solves the omitted block by exact rational linear programming, yielding a polynomial-time one-block elbow. A concrete serialized parser, generator, executable checker, and their end-to-end refinement proof remain open.

body.related_work: Shridharan and Iyengar motivate the problem most directly: their admissible canonical program class contains the forgetful image of \(\mathfrak I_{q,k}^{\ge3}\), while their exact linear and quadratic subfamily is incomparable with the headline class because the latter contains genuine degree-at-least-three objectives and excludes one- and two-component inputs. Their higher-degree guarantee is stationary-point convergence; the exact-width theorem strictly tightens that guarantee only on the common explicit bounded-width image. The secondary binary result is different: without assuming width, it enumerates complete vertex lists for only \(\ell-1\) query-relevant original blocks and handles the last by exact rational linear programming, becoming polynomial-time at \(\ell=1\). Duarte et al.'s discrete causal polynomial-program class also strictly contains this image because it permits broader graphs, real input tables, and unbounded scalar width; the exact-width theorem tightens epsilon-sharp output to exact rational sharpness only on the shared subclass and does not subsume their admissible class. Zaffalon, Antonucci, and Cabañas establish the quasi-Markovian credal correspondence, while Zaffalon et al. show that ordinary polytree structure does not make exact credal causal inference tractable in general. Dechter supplies the standard induced-width elimination and backpointer machinery; no new elimination rule is claimed. Sachs et al. supply response-function matrices and tight symbolic certificates for a linear class, and Li, Passmore, and Paulson supply the skeptical producer--checker architecture. Arroyo et al. address response-state explosion through single-intervention column generation under a different representation; the present secondary result retains fully explicit response columns and makes no column-generation claim. Alvarez and Ferrando's recent dynamic-regime recursion occupies rectangular chain-style backward induction but not the canonical response-width kernel. The causaloptim interface of Jonzon, Sachs, and Gabriel is the prospective consumer, contingent on a future eligible-input exporter.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The feasible response masses range over real H-polytopes; rationality is a derived property of their extreme points, not a restriction of the compatible-SCM class. The primary width bound is representation-sensitive and applies only after every canonical response coordinate, raw equality, nonnegativity record, query monomial, and decomposition bag is charged to \(B\). It does not transfer to implicit response columns or arbitrary algebraic rewrites. The secondary binary algorithm drops the width requirement but still requires the full explicit representation; its exponent depends on the number \(\ell-1\) of enumerated relevant blocks. Fixing \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is essential because optimization over a rational statistical confidence region can have irrational endpoints. A positive observed table does not justify strictly positive endpoint response masses.
body.honest_scope: The proved mathematical endpoint results are distinct from executable serialized refinement. The abstract support and separator verifier is specified mathematically; the serialized parser, generator completeness proof, executable checker, adversarial corruption tests, and end-to-end refinement bit bound remain open in \(\text{oeq:executable-refinement}\). The exact endpoint and skeptical-certificate theorems apply to \(\mathfrak I_{q,k}^{\ge3}\); the one- and two-component reductions are statements over \(\mathfrak J_{q,k}\). The secondary theorem over \(\mathfrak J_2^{\mathrm{nw}}\) assumes no width bound, enumerates only \(\ell-1\) relevant-block vertex lists, and is polynomial-time when \(\ell=1\). The fully serialized fixture \(\mathsf F_\star\) fixes the graph, table, intervention, polynomial, decomposition, endpoint masses, and replay obligations. The result excludes hardness, implicit column generation, statistical projection, new elimination machinery, benchmark gains, and any claim that causaloptim already implements the fallback.
